lesson_title: Buy Low, Sell Higher: How a Shop Makes Profit
hook_text: A shirt sells for R1 200 with a 50 percent mark-up. What did it cost? It is not R600.
clip_script: A spaza shop buys chips from a wholesaler. Is it poorer? No. It swapped money for chips worth the same. The chips are an asset: trading stock. Only when a packet is sold does something happen, and it happens twice. Heads: the customer pays the selling price, money in, sales. Tails: the packet leaves the shelf at what the shop paid, cost of sales. The gap is gross profit. Now the trap. A shirt sells for R1 200 with a 50 percent mark-up. Most people say it cost R600. Wrong. The 50 percent was added to the cost, so the selling price is 150 parts of cost. 1 200 divided by 150, times 100: R800. Check it: 800 plus half of 800 is 1 200. And if the owner takes that shirt home? Drawings, at cost: R800, not R1 200, because nothing was sold.
visual_style: A spaza shop shelf with price tags flipping between cost and selling price, a spinning coin labelled heads: sales and tails: cost of sales, and an on-screen fraction 1 200 × 100 ÷ 150.
mood: Sharp, practical, a little mischievous at the trap.
pacing: Brisk shop scene, a deliberate pause before the R800 reveal, quick close on drawings.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and calculate five cost prices without falling into the trap.
